clue.text: Fellow I shall cut short, inviting me in for a feed

indicators.note: inviting the word me in means taking it inside the trimmed 'I shall'
cut short tells us to drop the last letter of the word shall

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man announces that he will invite someone round for a meal, though his invitation is a bit abrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feed' is the noun here, food for animals or crops, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish meal is ground fish used as animal or plant food, a kind of feed.

clue.text: Sack cunning crawler

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
fly is informal British for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: A sly sycophant gets dismissed from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a toady, but here it is an insect; fly meaning shrewd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefly is a luminous beetle, an insect that can crawl.

clue.text: It's apparent doctor left, in attempt to reach the other side

indicators.note: in says doctor and left go inside the spiritualist sitting

parts.words: attempt to reach the other side
parts.note: a seance is a sitting to contact the dead on the other side
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor has gone, it seems, in trying to cross over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other side' is the spirit world in spiritualist talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward appearance, something that is apparent rather than real.

clue.text: Stuff written up on one Nobel prizewinner

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means the word is set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Material is written about one winner of a Nobel Prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns CRAM into MARC; Guglielmo Marconi won the physics Nobel in 1909.
explanation.definitionFit: Marconi, pioneer of radio, shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics.

clue.text: Taking an eternity arriving, say, being held up

indicators.note: being held says the turned example sits inside the arrival word

parts.note: coming along means arriving, so along stands for it

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the example word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A person arrives so slowly, being delayed, that it seems to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top; 'arriving' stands for 'coming along'.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-long means lasting an age, so taking what feels like an eternity.

clue.text: Brief time out, and top worker's called back in

indicators.note: in says the turned worker goes inside the top

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.note: called back says the worker's name is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone takes a short break, and the best employee gets summoned back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top worker' reads as the best employee, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep, a brief break from waking life.

clue.text: It's heavenly, in case Alice is worried about that

indicators.note: about says the shuffled name surrounds the other piece
worried suggests disturbed, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters of the name, to be shuffled
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A girl called Alice frets about something heavenly in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like a container signal but is the synonym piece, meaning 'for fear that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means of the sky or heaven, a direct synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Deleting last list of facts I had, with nothing on paper

indicators.note: deleting last says the final letter of the list word is dropped

parts.note: a table is an arranged list of facts or figures
O looks like zero, nothing
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone removes the final item from a factual list, leaving nothing on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on paper' tempts as a phrase meaning 'in theory', but 'paper' alone is the definition, a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper of small page size, so a paper.

clue.text: That's very long to stay on the outside and win

indicators.note: the yearning word stays outside and wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to long for is to ache for
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Something lasting very long is kept outside and then triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is the verb, to yearn; 'That's' is i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to succeed in gaining something, as in to win a prize.

clue.text: So poor mum feels sorry, all finally lost

definitions.text: So poor mum feels sorry, all finally lost

indicators.note: poor signals that the remaining letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged
all finally lost means every one of the three words loses its last letter, here M, S and Y

explanation.surface: A mother, hard up and having lost everything, feels contrite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all finally lost' cuts MUM, FEELS, SORRY to MU, FEEL, SORR; 'poor' shuffles MUFEELSORR. The whole clue then describes a mother full of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother who feels sorry is full of regret, the state of being contrite.

clue.text: Decorative inlays around centre line

indicators.note: around here means turned around, so the centre word is read backwards

parts.note: a hub is the centre, as of a wheel or activity

explanation.surface: Ornamental inlay work runs around a central line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' here signals turning round, not enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Buhl is ornamental inlay of brass, tortoiseshell and similar on furniture, named after the cabinetmaker Boulle.

clue.text: Act instinctively and make progress, without looking back?

definitions.meaning: to act on instinct, trusting one's gut rather than reasoning
a cryptic picture of walking straight ahead, guided only by the front of one's face

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to trust one's instincts and, literally, to go straight forward.

clue.text: Dragging family into aspect of Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: into says family goes inside the Chinese principle

parts.note: yang is the active, masculine principle in Chinese philosophy
kin means family

explanation.surface: A family is being pulled into a strand of Eastern thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanking is pulling sharply, a synonym of dragging.

clue.text: It'll be a drag if one fails to abstain

definitions.text: It'll be a drag if one fails to abstain

parts.words: It'll be a drag if one fails to abstain
parts.note: a drag is a puff on a cigarette, which such a person would take only by failing in their resolve

explanation.surface: Missing out on abstinence would be a bore for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' reads as a tedious thing but means a pull on a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-smoker abstains from tobacco, so a drag would mean a lapse.

clue.text: Objects to alien way of thinking

parts.note: to object is to mind, so objects means minds
ET is the film alien, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a strange mode of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a plural noun but is the verb: he objects, he minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed set of attitudes, a habitual way of thinking.

clue.text: Sail in a ketch, initially packing bait for fishing

indicators.note: packing says the bait word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a spinner is a revolving lure used in angling

indicators.note: initially says just the first letter of ketch is used

explanation.surface: Aboard a small sailing boat, someone first loads up fishing bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' puts A and K inside SPINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a large triangular sail set forward on a yacht.

clue.text: One's made to go straight

parts.note: the surface suggests a reformed criminal, but the reading is of a route you make when heading somewhere directly

explanation.definitionFit: You make a beeline when heading somewhere by the most direct path.

clue.text: Expatiate, or blow up?

definitions.meaning: to speak or write at length on a subject

explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge on a topic is to expatiate, and to enlarge a picture is to blow it up.

clue.text: Spotted insect that's ugly, and bad for cultivation

indicators.note: cultivation means working the ground over, so these letters are turned over and rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A spotted bug that's unpleasant to look at is bad news for crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder: UGLY plus BAD is shuffled by 'for cultivation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybug, the American name for a ladybird, is a red beetle with black spots.

clue.text: Slope off around four to write a letter

indicators.note: around says the shuffled slope wraps round the Roman four
off means gone wrong, so the letters of slope are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters of slope, to be shuffled
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away at about four o'clock to write a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' means a consonant of a phonetic type, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plosive is a consonant sound such as P or B, so a letter of that class.

clue.text: Some copy to be included — keep overlooking this?

indicators.note: to be included says the copy word goes inside the portion word

parts.note: part means some, a portion
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Part of a manuscript is to be added, and someone keeps glancing past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' is not the verb but a castle stronghold, whose top wall looks out over the parapet.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is the low protective wall along the top of a castle keep, overlooking the ground below.

clue.text: As Model T. may appear, if one's been kept?

definitions.text: As Model T. may appear, if one's been kept?

indicators.note: may appear differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters of the car's name, as fodder
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old Ford car looks like a relic if somebody has kept one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear' shuffles MODELT plus I, the one kept among them; the whole clue describes an old Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time means belonging to former days, as a preserved vintage car looks.

clue.text: In a position to have made a choice

definitions.meaning: voted into an office or post

explanation.definitionFit: Elected means both voted into office and having chosen to do something.

clue.text: Exploited having started the knees-up, perhaps

parts.note: to have started a dance is to have led it
a knees-up is British slang for a lively party; a merry dance is one example

explanation.surface: Someone took advantage after kicking off the party.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a British term for a boisterous party with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have led someone a merry dance is to have strung them along, taking advantage of them.

clue.text: Eats a maggot?

definitions.meaning: eats as a noun is slang for food
an insect larva, of which a maggot is one example

explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food and also a larva such as a maggot.

clue.text: Deal with deliveries missed, maybe making dismissals

definitions.text: Deal with deliveries missed, maybe making dismissals

parts.words: Deal with deliveries missed, maybe making dismissals
parts.note: in cricket, the fielder behind the stumps gathers balls the batsman misses and may stump or catch him out

explanation.surface: A postal worker handles lost parcels and sacks people.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's balls are deliveries, and the player who fields behind the batsman's stumps catches what is missed and can dismiss the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep wicket is to field behind the stumps in cricket, collecting missed balls and taking catches or stumpings.

clue.text: A bit of breakfast, pub sandwiches, for the poor bloke

indicators.note: sandwiches means the pub word encloses the breakfast item

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a room in one
an egg is one item of a breakfast

explanation.surface: A pub serves breakfast food and sandwiches to a down-and-out man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like a food noun but is the verb: the pub holds the egg between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is a destitute person who asks for alms, a poor fellow.

clue.text: On move three, led to expose king

indicators.note: on the move suggests letters shifting position, so three and led are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: In a chess game, the third move leads to the king being left in check.
explanation.walkthrough: THREE and LED are shuffled together to give the Saxon king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an English king of the Anglo-Saxon period.
